newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes softer at 1,600-1,610 to dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes softer at 1,600-1,610 to dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed a touch softer at 1,600-1,610 per dollar from 1,590-1,600 in morning trade as demand for foreign currency rose on the interbank market, dealers said.
"Dollar demand rose slightly, pushing the lev down some 10 from morning levels in lively trade," one dealer said.

The central bank was the main dollar buyer today, as it has been in the past few days, keeping the lev fairly stable amid increased dollar supply. Central bank officials were not available for comment.

Foreign currency supply from clients has risen this week on expectations of a stable or a firmer lev after the interim government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) announced a $650 million financial accord on Monday.
There were rumours in the market that Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim might start bidding for some $12 million in the next few days to meet payments to crude oil suppliers, dealers said.

"But the general feeling is that those bids are not likely to increase pressure on the lev dramatically because they would be met probably either by large state banks with good foreign currency liquidity or the central bank," another dealer said.
